decision_theory_boundaries.actual_hard_rule: d_theta(x)=argmax_r z_theta,r(x), with a fixed tie rule. The token Born scores p_rt produce alpha_rt and then class logits; they are not a joint class POVM, class posterior probabilities, or a stochastic draw of d_theta.
decision_theory_boundaries.population_quantities: For pi_r=P(Y=r), q_r=P(d_theta(X)=r), t_r=P(Y=r,d_theta(X)=r), population F1_r=2t_r/(pi_r+q_r), with a stated zero-denominator convention. Population Macro is the mean over the fixed 40 labels. Population CE is E[-log softmax(z_theta(X))_Y], a distinct objective.
decision_theory_boundaries.empirical_quantities: Reported Macro uses finite confusion counts divided by their empirical denominators. At fixed TP_r and FN_r, F1_r=2TP_r/(2TP_r+FN_r+FP_r) varies only through FP_r. That is exact metric accounting, not a theorem about learned measurement geometry or population risk.

exact_missing_premise.statement: An independently task-supported condition on the joint prepared-state, utility and class-margin distribution that predicts selective changes of hard false positives under a specified label-blind measurement/attention intervention, while accounting for true-positive effects and errors transferred to every competing class.
exact_missing_premise.why_it_is_needed: A measurement can change token scores without moving a class margin; it can change a margin without changing argmax; and an argmax change can remove one class's FP while adding another's. The reported finite FP accounting does not supply the joint law needed to predict a beneficial task-level redistribution.
